signals.notes: Direction is stated relative to PRICE: near-zero supply growth is price-supportive. World gross mine production 2026e 23,500 kt, +0.2% vs an implied 2025 of 23,450 kt [Cochilco forecast, 2026-08-11 relay]. Competing estimate: ICSG April-2026 growth of +1.6% applied to USGS MCS 2026 world 2025 of 23,000 kt = 23,368 kt (DERIVED, mixed base). The two are NOT independent - both anchor near 23 Mt - so their 0.56% dispersion understates disagreement; the growth rates differ by 1.4pp (+1.6% vs +0.2%), an ~8x relative spread. Required series copper.mine-prepolicy-supply is UNUSABLE (no_pool, no accepted vintage); this row does not satisfy it and cannot lift sufficiency. Primary-source production coverage measured at 0.0% (0 kt / 23,500 kt): every figure is a trade-press relay, five direct primary retrievals failed (2x HTTP 403, 3x unreadable PDF).

The composition finding, not the headline. ICSG Q1-2026 preliminary: total world mine production 'basically flat', but copper CONCENTRATES -1.1% y/y while SX-EW cathode +3.3% y/y. SX-EW is leached and electro-won at the mine and never enters a smelter, so it does not relieve smelter feed. A flat world total therefore coexists with a falling smeltable stream. Unvintaged secondary relay of ICSG data; ICSG's own bulletin PDFs were retrieved but unreadable.

TC/RC = the fee a smelter earns for turning concentrate into metal, per dry metric tonne of concentrate; NEGATIVE means the smelter pays the miner. 2026 annual benchmark US$0/t and 0 US cents/lb (Antofagasta with a Chinese smelter, recorded Jan-2026), the lowest annual benchmark on record, vs US$21.25/t for 2025. Spot: -US$126.80/t at end-June 2026; -US$182.14/dmt on 2026-08-21 [SMM]. COPPER FAMILY RULE APPLIED: this is NOT a second vote for the mine disruptions already emitted - it is the price tag on the same concentrate shortfall, and it sits in the same primary-supply cluster so the compiler aggregates it by median strength rather than counting it twice. Attribution (MODULE_RULES 4a): concentrate output -1.1% y/y (Q1-2026) against China refined output +7.4% y/y (Jan-Apr 2026) = an ~8.5pp feed-vs-capacity gap, but NO elasticity of spot TC to a 1pp feed gap was sourced on any basis, so 0% of the -US$182.14/dmt level is arithmetically attributed and 100% is residual. The feed gap is the obvious candidate cause and is NOT proven here. Required series copper.concentrate-tcrc is UNUSABLE: only one current assessor was reachable, so the profile-required dispersion is not measurable.

Chile, ~24% of world mine supply. Cochilco 2026 forecast 5,270 kt, -2.6% vs a derived 2025 of 5,411 kt, cut ~30 kt from its May-2026 forecast of 5.3 Mt. H1-2026 cumulative output -6.6% y/y with Codelco -10% y/y. Attribution (4a): H1-2026 -6.6% x an INFERRED H1-2025 base of 2,706 kt (half of FY-2025 5,411 kt; actual H1-2025 print NOT sourced, and a 50/50 seasonal split is an assumption) = -179 kt of the -141 kt full-year decline forecast -> 127% of the full-year decline is explained by H1 alone; residual +38 kt with the WRONG SIGN, i.e. the 5,270 kt forecast REQUIRES H2 to run +38 kt above year-ago. Falsifier, dated and cheap: July and August INE prints below year-ago make 5,270 kt unreachable.

The opposing fact, emitted separately rather than netted against the decline row. Chile INE total June-2026 output 447,294 t, +5.1% y/y - the first month of the H2 recovery the Cochilco forecast requires. Composition: Escondida 111,400 t (+45.8% y/y) offsetting Codelco 114,400 t (-4.8% y/y) and Collahuasi 34,900 t (+1.7% y/y). Bearish for price because more supply arriving is price-negative. ONE month is not a trend: two further prints (July, August) decide whether the -2.6% full-year figure holds or worsens.

Grasberg 2026 guidance ~1.0 billion lb copper = ~454 kt (1,000,000,000 / 2,204.62 lb per t), 'similar to 2025' and ~35% below the pre-incident estimate, after ~800,000 t of wet material entered the block cave on 2025-09-08 and force majeure was declared; full restart has slipped. Indonesia country total already fell 1,010 kt (2024) -> 710 kt (2025e), -29.7%. CONTESTED SIZE, not averaged: one relay states a ~270 kt loss in 2026; the '35% below plan' statement on a 454 kt actual implies a 698 kt plan and a 244 kt loss - a 26 kt (~11%) gap left unresolved because neither primary document was readable. The conservative 244 kt is carried where one number is needed. Grasberg loss is concentrate, so it hits the same stream as copper-concentrate-stream-contracting.

Kamoa-Kakula (DRC) 2026 guidance now 290-310 kt, against 380-420 kt in the one PRIMARY document I retrieved and could read [Ivanhoe Mines news release, 2025-12-03 - now SUPERSEDED]. Midpoint to midpoint = -100 kt. H1-2026 actual ~135.7 kt (Q2 64,328 t) after a 2025-05-20 seismic event at Kakula and nine lost mining days at Kakula plus seven at Kamoa in Q2-2026 from industrial action. 2027 guidance previously 500-540 kt. Because the Ivanhoe release is superseded and carries no current-period actuals, it contributes 0 kt to the 0.0% primary-coverage numerator. DRC's 2026 COUNTRY total was not published in any source read - a ~14%-of-world hole.

The offsetting fact, stated separately rather than netted. ICSG Q1-2026: China and the DRC together - 60% of world mine production - raised combined output +9% y/y, while production EXCLUDING those two countries fell 1.4% y/y. These are the tonnes holding the world total flat rather than down, which is why this row is bearish for price and contradicts the two rows above. Two qualifiers travel with it: much of the DRC increment is SX-EW cathode that never reaches a smelter, and the concentration of all growth into two origins is a supply-SECURITY question owned by orb 04 and deliberately not scored here.

Explicit gap row so the absence is machine-visible. Zero strength, neutral, non-voting. The origin-level pre-policy bridge does NOT close for Chile, Peru, DRC or Indonesia: domestic absorption (smelter and refinery intake) was not sourced for any of them, so every origin's pre-policy exportable supply is NOT COMPUTABLE, not zero. The world row closes only by borrowing refined usage from commodity-demand-inventory as a cross-reference. MEASURED OPACITY passed to scripts/commodity_analytical_contracts.py: primary_coverage_pct = 0.0 (0 kt / 23,500 kt; five primary retrievals failed - 2x HTTP 403, 3x unreadable binary PDF); estimate_dispersion_pct = 0.56 ((23,500-23,368)/23,434 x 100 on the world 2026 total, with a non-independence caveat and matched-basis alternatives of 1.93% on the 2025 level and a 1.4pp growth-rate gap); release_cycles_late = 1 (ICSG Monthly Copper Bulletin, monthly cadence, latest evidenced data month May-2026 vs expected June-2026 at a 2026-08-28 decision date). Coverage below 70% => HIGH opacity => supply-demand directional-conviction score capped at 45. Restrictions, sanctions, chokepoints and rerouting are excluded here by design and belong to commodity-supply-security.

Scrap-based refined output is the supply stream that is actually growing, and it is price-negative. ICSG Jan-May 2026: secondary refined production +5.6% y/y against primary refined +2.4% y/y; May alone +5.5% y/y, the increase mainly from China. Secondary's share of world refined output rose from 17.3% (Jan-May 2025) to 17.8% (Jan-May 2026). India May-2026 output estimated +30% y/y on the Adani Mundra refinery ramp. ICSG April-2026 forecasts secondary +5.7% in 2027. Derived tonnage used in the world bridge: 17.8% x a derived world refined 2026e of 28,656 kt = 5,101 kt - the build is 28,110 kt 2025 usage base x 1.016 = 28,560 kt usage, plus ICSG's stated 2026 surplus of 96 kt. NOT COUNTED anywhere: direct-melt scrap, remelted without passing through a refinery, which never enters the refined balance and which no source reached puts a number on. Required series copper.scrap-supply is UNUSABLE (no_pool; no absolute tonnage, no grade split, no geography split).

China copper-scrap imports 1,240 kt in H1-2026, +8.3% y/y (implying an H1-2025 base of ~1,145 kt). Scrap reached 25.2% of China's refined-copper feedstock in H1-2026, explicitly because concentrate availability tightened and spot treatment charges fell further below zero - i.e. smelters substituted toward scrap because concentrate became unaffordable. SECTION 9 ELIMINATION NOTE: these imported tonnes are other origins' scrap and are a TRANSFER, not new world supply; they cancel on world consolidation and are not added to the world bridge. Any US export-restriction or Southeast-Asia rerouting angle on this trade belongs to commodity-supply-security (orb 04) and is deliberately not applied here.

The constraint on the substitution the row above measures, emitted separately rather than netted. The refined-minus-scrap price spread - the discount scrap trades at to refined metal, which is what makes scrap worth feeding - 'narrowed considerably' in June 2026 as scrap prices held up on tight spot availability. A narrower spread mechanically reduces the incentive to substitute scrap for concentrate, so it is price-supportive. DIRECTION ONLY: no numeric spread assessment (RMB/t or USD/t) was obtained, and only one assessor was reachable, so the profile's required dispersion on scrap estimates is NOT MEASURABLE. Strength held low (0.25) for that reason; this row must not be read as a sized effect.
